text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.3% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 11%. The primary driver appears to be the broader collapse in oil prices: US crude has dropped from around $146 per barrel two weeks ago to $99.64 today, a roughly 32% plunge. Refiners and oil producers like ConocoPhillips are directly exposed to the price their product commands—lower crude means lower revenue and margins, even if their operations haven't changed.

The company reported third-quarter earnings on November 5th, which may have set expectations for the market right as oil prices began their steeper descent. Geopolitical tension around Iran (noted in today's news) typically supports oil prices by creating supply uncertainty, but the fact that diplomatic hopes appear dim suggests the market isn't pricing in a near-term disruption—leaving crude vulnerable to other downward pressures.
